title: Clarify scope and acceptance for structured-output defaults across deployment modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The PRD proposes default changes to structured-output (JSON / function-like responses) behavior so that hosted, dedicated, and private deployments produce consistent schema envelopes and error semantics. This ticket coordinates cross-team alignment to avoid breaking existing customers and to surface legal/security concerns for data retention and PII in structured outputs.

Scope clarified here:
- In-scope: default schema envelope format, error code surface, function-calling fallback semantics, SDK serialization behavior, and migration strategy for existing customers.
- Out-of-scope: model-level output distribution changes, developer opt-in flag implementation for advanced schema transforms (handled in follow-ups).

Goal: Obtain explicit sign-offs from Engineering, Design, and Legal on the acceptance criteria below, finalize a rollout plan with feature flags, and lock the PRD so it can be scheduled for release in api-2026.04.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering sign-off: compatibility tests pass for hosted/dedicated/private with <=0.5% failing requests on a 7-day rolling window vs current prod for top 10 customer prompts (regression acceptance)
Design sign-off: developer-facing examples and SDK surface documented with Figma screenshots and code samples for Python/JS in the Console and API docs
Legal sign-off: data-retention & PII guidance approved; confirmation that structured outputs do not introduce new audit obligations for customers in EU/UK
Migration plan: automatic compatibility layer with opt-out header for 90-day grace period; a clear deprecation notice and customer communication template
Rollout gating: feature flag per deployment mode + canary cohort (5% traffic) with metrics dashboard monitored (errors, latency, changed-token-rate), and automatic rollback threshold defined
Test coverage: end-to-end tests added to infra canary harness and unit tests for SDK serializers across 3 runtimes
Observability: Console dashboard tile and alert configured for new schema mismatch errors and per-route token delta
Docs & changelog: PRD-linked docs merged before release and 'breaking change' notice prepared for enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private contracts
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting notes — aligned scope with ENG (Marco Chen), DES (Sofia Nguyen), and Legal (Priya Rao). Action: ENG to prototype compatibility layer; DES to produce developer copy examples by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-03: Marco (ENG) posted initial prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/structured-output/proto-compat (see PR #246). Prototype shows serializer shim + header opt-out. Request: add e2e scenarios for private deployments behind VPC.

2026-03-04: Sofia (DES) uploaded Figma frames: https://figma.com/file/XYZ/structured-output-examples — requested feedback on UX for error messaging. PM note: prefer concise error text to reduce downstream parsing complexity.

2026-03-06: Legal (Priya) asked for a short brief on PII surface area and suggested adding a requirement to redact recognized PII by default in structured outputs for hosted mode. Action: PM to scope redaction as separate follow-up; for now Legal wants a mitigations doc included in the PRD.
2026-03-08: Diego (assignee) updated acceptance criteria to include 'changed-token-rate' metric to detect verbosity regressions. ENG to add telemetry by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-09: Action items consolidated: (1) ENG add canary dashboard & rollback thresholds; (2) DES finalize examples and copy; (3) Legal confirm wording for enterprise notice. Next checkpoint 2026-03-11.
